to spring up (e.g. an idea, emotions, clouds)

example.romaji: koko kara onsen ga waite iru.
example.hiragana: ここからおんせんがわいている。
example.english: Hot spring water wells up from here.

records.meaning: to well up, to spring forth, to gush out
meaningAliases: to feel emotions (e.g. joy, bravery, etc.)
to spring up (e.g. an idea, emotions, clouds)

example.romaji: yama no chuufuku kara shimizu ga wakideteiru.
example.hiragana: やまのちゅうふくからしみずがわきでている。
example.english: Spring water gushes out from the mountainside.

records.meaning: to surge, to well up (emotions, ideas)

example.romaji: hanashi wo kiite kyoumi ga waita.
example.hiragana: はなしをきいてきょうみがわいた。
example.english: Hearing the story sparked my interest.

example.romaji: washokki de shokuji wo suru.
example.hiragana: わしょっきでしょくじをする。
example.english: To eat using Japanese tableware.

example.romaji: washokki wa ryouri wo utsukushiku misete kureru.
example.hiragana: わしょっきはりょうりをうつくしくみせてくれる。
example.english: Japanese tableware makes food look beautiful.

meaningAliases: kanji created in Japan (as opposed to China)

example.romaji: waji wa nihon no fuudo ya bunka wo han'eishite tsukurareta.
example.hiragana: わじはにほんのふうどやぶんかをはんえいしてつくられた。
example.english: Japanese-made characters were created to reflect Japan's natural environment and culture.

meaningAliases: kanji created in Japan (as opposed to China)

example.romaji: waji no naka ni wa, chuugoku de wa tsukawarenai kanji ga ooku fukumareteiru.
example.hiragana: わじのなかには、ちゅうごくではつかわれないかんじがおおくふくまれている。
example.english: Among Japanese-made characters, there are many kanji that are not used in China.

example.romaji: heianjidai ni waji toshite kana ga hattatsu shita.
example.hiragana: へいあんじだいにわじとしてかながはったつした。
example.english: Kana developed as Japanese writing during the Heian period.

example.romaji: waji to kanji wo kumiawaseta hyouki wa nihongo no tokuchou da.
example.hiragana: わじとかんじをくみあわせたひょうきはにほんごのとくちょうだ。
example.english: The combination of kana and kanji in writing is a characteristic feature of Japanese.

example.romaji: komonjo ni wa waji to kanbun ga konzai shiteiru.
example.hiragana: こもんじょにはわじとかんぶんがこんざいしている。
example.english: Old documents contain a mix of Japanese writing and classical Chinese text.

records.meaning: to accept rationally; to come to terms with; to take a pragmatic view

example.romaji: warikitte kangaeru.
example.hiragana: わりきってかんがえる。
example.english: To think about it rationally.

records.meaning: to accept rationally; to come to terms with; to take a pragmatic view

example.romaji: shigoto to warikitte yaru shikanai.
example.hiragana: しごととわりきってやるしかない。
example.english: I have no choice but to accept it as work and get on with it.

records.meaning: to accept rationally; to come to terms with; to take a pragmatic view

example.romaji: kako no koto wa warikitte, mae ni susumou.
example.hiragana: かこのことはわりきって、まえにすすもう。
example.english: Let's put the past behind us and move forward.

records.meaning: to divide evenly; to divide without a remainder

example.romaji: 10 wa 5 de warikireru.
example.hiragana: 10は5でわりきれる。
example.english: 10 is evenly divisible by 5.

records.meaning: to divide evenly; to divide without a remainder

example.romaji: 7 wa 2 de warikirenai.
example.hiragana: 7は2でわりきれない。
example.english: 7 is not evenly divisible by 2.

records.meaning: to divide evenly; to divide without a remainder

example.romaji: warikirenai suu wa shousuuten de hyoujisareru.
example.hiragana: わりきれないすうはしょうすうてんでひょうじされる。
example.english: Numbers that don't divide evenly are displayed as decimals.

records.meaning: looks interesting; looks like fun; sounds fun

example.hiragana: このきかくはおもしろそうだ。
